entities.summary: Ctesias (b. 500 BCE, Knidos) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Knidos. He served as a chronicler and historian for the Persian Empire, recording the accounts of Alexander the Great's conquests in his work “Histories”. Ctesias was a key figure in the transmission of Greek knowledge to the East, and his writings played a significant role in shaping the cultural and intellectual landscape of the ancient world. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Western historiography and the study of ancient civilizations. The historian Herodotus, who predated Ctesias, is also known to have influenced his work. Ctesias' own experiences as a diplomat and traveler in the Persian Empire and the Indus Valley contributed to his unique perspective on the cultures and peoples he encountered.
